page: Microsoft Azure E4ns_v6 is an Env6-family virtual server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). No local storage or GPUs are included, though the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is average at 1916.18, and the PassMark CPU score is average at 7245.74. However, multi-core stress-ng performance is weak at 3927.87, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also weak at 25.75 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is weak across both small cached blocks (304.17 GB/sec) and large uncached blocks (31.34 GB/sec read, 23.07 GB/sec write). For lightweight AI tasks, the server achieves an average prompt processing speed of 472.46 tokens/sec and text generation speed of 192.82 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM, but drops to a weak 29.47 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ns_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated Intel hardware, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high multi-core compute density. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external Premium Storage. Given its average single-core performance, average static web serving throughput of 7.48 GB/sec, and weak database operations score (2482.35), this server is best suited for memory-optimized applications, network-optimized routing, caching layers, and lightweight web serving rather than heavy multi-threaded database or compute-bound processing.
